purpose: Translate public-sector AI directives and action plans into named obligations, owners, records, deadlines, and review decisions instead of treating plans as general aspirations.
staffSummary: Build M29 around one consequential utility situation and one decision: Determine which actions a public utility should take now, monitor, or route for legal and policy review. The learner must leave with a usable public-sector AI action register, not a collection of definitions.
openingSituation: A public agency announces an AI action plan, and departments are unsure which items are binding, advisory, funded, applicable, or assigned.
learnerDecision: Determine which actions a public utility should take now, monitor, or route for legal and policy review.
analogy: A consent-decree schedule works because each action has an owner, evidence, and date. A public AI plan needs the same operating translation.
learnerOutcomes: Explain AI Action Plans and Public-Sector Requirements in plain English and connect it to a real water, wastewater, stormwater, or One Water decision.
Distinguish strategy, action plan, directive, requirement, recommendation, milestone, evidence, and accountable owner without using one term to hide several different jobs.
Analyze the module situation, identify missing evidence, and name the professional consequence of a weak decision.
Compare how the same question changes across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater, administration, engineering, finance, technology, and public leadership.

Evaluate sources, assumptions, limitations, permissions, and human authority using this boundary: Keep federal, state, local, and organizational authority separate. Use a state requirement only when scope, applicability, and effective date are explicitly approved for the course.
Create a usable public-sector AI action register with evidence, roles, limits, review steps, and the next accountable action.
Defend the recommendation to Foundation, Practitioner, and Leader audiences while keeping disagreement and uncertainty visible.
curriculumOutcomes: Give AI Action Plans and Public-Sector Requirements one clear learning job inside Governance, Security and Provenance.
Connect the module to a consequential decision and the public-sector AI action register.
Preserve current content, proposals, enhancements, and contributor records by stable identifier.
Separate verified evidence, Hardeep positions, expert interpretation, instructional scenarios, and unresolved questions.
Create an explicit bridge to the preceding and following modules without duplicating their work.
marketingOutcomes: Describe the practical value as helping a learner make and explain this decision: Determine which actions a public utility should take now, monitor, or route for legal and policy review.
Name the public-sector AI action register as the visible result of the module.
Do not promise savings, compliance, certification, safety, performance, implementation success, or career outcomes without separately approved evidence.
definitionOfDone: The learner explains the core distinctions, completes the required evidence and decision activities, passes distributed checks, saves a complete public-sector AI action register, and names the next accountable action.
